metadata.title: From Promise to Experience
metadata.thesis: Airtel’s premium positioning and Jio’s ecosystem scale create different service expectations and execution risks.
metadata.frameworkStatus: The 7Ps, GAP diagnostics and service blueprints are managerial interpretations reconstructed from the supplied presentation information base.
metadata.recommendationStatus: Controls, recovery responses, roadmap horizons, priorities and KPIs are proposals, not measured operator practices, announced commitments or demonstrated effects.
metadata.journeyStatus: Journey stages describe analytical failure hypotheses, not measured failure frequencies.
metadata.sourceLimitation: The original PowerPoint is unavailable; the 15-slide structure follows the supplied Markdown reconstruction.
metadata.surveyProvenance: Calculated from the supplied workbook; customer-response origin confirmed by the project owner.

research.title: The service promise
research.question: How do Airtel and Jio differ across the 7Ps, and which differences could matter for subscriber lifetime value?
research.framework: The extended services marketing mix connects commercial positioning with people, processes and visible service cues.
research.evidence: Operator reporting establishes monetisation and scale, while the reconstructed presentation supplies the strategic comparison.
research.limitation: Positioning does not demonstrate superior delivery, and the supplied survey does not measure customer lifetime value.

research.title: The evidence boundary
research.question: Which SERVQUAL dimensions have defensible evidence, and where are the measurements incomplete?
research.framework: SERVQUAL distinguishes reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy and tangibles.
research.evidence: Survey items measure customer perceptions, while Opensignal measures defined network experiences independently.
research.limitation: Missing expectation questions and physical-tangibles items prevent classical SERVQUAL gaps or a complete validated five-dimension score.

research.title: The execution gap
research.question: Where could the five service-quality gaps arise in Airtel’s system, and which operating controls could reduce them?
research.framework: The GAP Model links customer knowledge, service standards, delivery, communication and perceived experience.
research.evidence: Dated network measures and the presentation’s operating hypotheses identify questions for local investigation.
research.limitation: Public national averages and the survey cannot establish an operator’s internal root causes or local process performance.

research.title: The recovery test
research.question: Where can mobile and broadband journeys fail, and how should fairness shape the recovery?
research.framework: Service blueprints expose handoffs, while distributive, procedural and interactional justice guide remedies.
research.evidence: The reconstructed journeys identify failure modes and eligible survey responses describe support and recovery perceptions.
research.limitation: The playbook is a proposed design; observed survey associations cannot prove that a remedy will improve retention.

ps.label: Product
ps.airtel: Premium postpaid, convergence, roaming and Fast Lane express a proposition built around higher-value customer needs.
ps.jio: True 5G, JioFiber, JioAirFiber and entertainment or cloud services connect customers to a broad digital ecosystem.
ps.difference: Airtel emphasizes premium value and convergence, while Jio emphasizes ecosystem attachment and broadband scale.
ps.expectation: The purchased plan, network feature and bundled benefit should work together in the customer’s actual context.
ps.dependency: Device compatibility, local coverage, provisioning and partner entitlement systems must agree on eligibility.
ps.failure: A plan is active but a promised network feature or bundled benefit remains unavailable.
ps.implication: Validate complete service blueprints before launch and give every entitlement exception one accountable owner.
ps.kpi: Proposed KPI: payment-to-entitlement success rate and unresolved entitlement exceptions.

ps.label: Price
ps.airtel: Higher reported mobile ARPU is consistent with Airtel’s premiumisation and higher-value customer mix.
ps.jio: Jio combines a lower reported mobile ARPU with a larger customer base and bundled ecosystem value.
ps.difference: Airtel seeks more monetisation per user, while Jio combines scale with rising monetisation.
ps.expectation: Customers choosing a premium proposition may expect its value to be visible in everyday service and recovery.
ps.dependency: Segment-level network, provisioning, support and recovery performance must be observable across the full journey.
ps.failure: A higher-value plan creates an expectation that inconsistent local delivery cannot meet.
ps.implication: Define postpaid service objectives and test whether the premium segment experiences the intended differentiation.
ps.kpi: Proposed KPI: postpaid customer effort, repeat contact, entitlement success and p90 recovery time.

ps.label: Place
ps.airtel: The Airtel App, retail stores, contact centres and roaming partnerships provide multiple access points.
ps.jio: MyJio, digital self-service, retail access and home-installation teams connect online and physical service.
ps.difference: Both are omnichannel; continuity of customer context is a more useful diagnostic than channel count alone.
ps.expectation: Moving from an app to a call or store should preserve the issue, evidence and promised next step.
ps.dependency: A common case identifier and diagnostic history must be accessible to every responsible channel.
ps.failure: Customers repeat their problem because channel handoffs lose history or ownership.
ps.implication: Make one case history available across channels and explicitly transfer responsibility at each handoff.
ps.kpi: Proposed KPI: context-preserving handoff rate and repeat contact within seven days.

ps.label: Promotion
ps.airtel: Premium network experience, convergence rewards and postpaid positioning raise the prominence of service quality.
ps.jio: 5G, affordability, entertainment and device bundles emphasize technology access and ecosystem value.
ps.difference: Airtel’s promise raises a quality reference point, while Jio’s promise broadens the range of benefits customers expect.
ps.expectation: Headline claims should remain accurate after location, device, software and plan conditions are considered.
ps.dependency: Marketing content must reflect verified product conditions and current eligibility information.
ps.failure: A broad promotional claim is interpreted as a guarantee in an unsupported customer context.
ps.implication: Place clear conditions and a device or location eligibility check beside the promise.
ps.kpi: Proposed KPI: eligibility-check completion and complaints linked to expectation mismatch.

ps.label: People
ps.airtel: A premium proposition makes frontline diagnostic competence, ownership and remedy authority especially visible.
ps.jio: Service at large scale requires consistent agent capability and a practical path for exceptions to reach an owner.
ps.difference: The presentation frames Airtel’s risk as inconsistent premium support and Jio’s risk as exception handling at volume.
ps.expectation: The person handling a problem should understand its context and be able to move it toward resolution.
ps.dependency: Agents need shared diagnostics, clear escalation paths and authority matched to the failure’s severity.
ps.failure: Script-bound support repeatedly escalates an issue without restoring service or explaining the next step.
ps.implication: Define remedy authority for recurring failure classes and coach for competent, respectful ownership.
ps.kpi: Proposed KPI: time to remedy, escalation rate and post-recovery satisfaction.

ps.label: Process
ps.airtel: Onboarding, postpaid upgrades, billing and home feasibility must consistently support the premium proposition.
ps.jio: The presentation describes automation as a strategic signal, but comparative straight-through performance is unverified.
ps.difference: Airtel must demonstrate disciplined execution, while Jio must keep automated journeys and exception recovery coherent at scale.
ps.expectation: Payment, activation, installation and support should complete without the customer coordinating internal systems.
ps.dependency: Billing, entitlement, provisioning, field scheduling and case management must share reliable state transitions.
ps.failure: A payment succeeds, a plan changes or an order is accepted without its dependent service becoming ready.
ps.implication: Monitor the end-to-end outcome and route broken handoffs into a visible recovery process.
ps.kpi: Proposed KPI: exception rate, payment-to-entitlement success and installation on the committed date.

ps.label: Physical Evidence
ps.airtel: Stores, bills, equipment, installation workmanship and app status make an intangible premium promise visible.
ps.jio: Apps, routers, set-top boxes and installation closeout provide visible cues across the home and digital ecosystem.
ps.difference: The relevant comparison is the clarity and consistency of service cues, not an established overall tangibles advantage.
ps.expectation: Bills, ticket timelines and installed equipment should clearly show what was delivered and what remains open.
ps.dependency: Customer-facing status must match backend state, while field teams verify and document installation quality.
ps.failure: Opaque status, unclear bills or poor router placement undermine trust despite an active connection.
ps.implication: Use clear status trackers, understandable bills and a customer-confirmed installation checklist.
ps.kpi: Proposed KPI: status accuracy, installation verification and repeat visits after closeout.

controls.title: Product ↔ Process
controls.question: Can every advertised entitlement be delivered in the customer’s actual device and location context?
controls.dependency: Pre-launch service blueprints and multi-system tests require one accountable entitlement owner.
controls.risk: An active plan with a missing benefit turns an internal integration defect into a broken customer promise.
controls.kpi: Proposed KPI: entitlement success rate and time to resolve entitlement exceptions.

controls.title: Price ↔ Reliability
controls.question: Does the postpaid or convergence segment experience the intended end-to-end service differentiation?
controls.dependency: Segment-level experience and recovery measurements must connect network delivery with provisioning and care.
controls.risk: Premium positioning becomes harder to sustain when daily service does not visibly justify the expectation.
controls.kpi: Proposed KPI: segment-level experience quality, customer effort and p90 recovery time.

controls.title: Promotion ↔ Local Reality
controls.question: Do promotional claims accurately reflect local coverage, device compatibility and plan eligibility?
controls.dependency: Location-aware messaging needs a maintained eligibility checker and plain-language conditions.
controls.risk: Customers may mistake a conditional feature claim for a promise that applies everywhere.
controls.kpi: Proposed KPI: eligibility accuracy and complaints associated with misleading expectations.

controls.title: Place ↔ Context
controls.question: Does customer history persist from app to contact centre to retail?
controls.dependency: Every channel must use a unified case identifier and a common diagnostic timeline.
controls.risk: Lost history creates repeated explanations, redundant diagnosis and unclear ownership.
controls.kpi: Proposed KPI: context-preserving transfers and repeat contact within seven days.

controls.title: People ↔ Recovery
controls.question: Can frontline staff resolve or compensate for defined failures without excessive escalation?
controls.dependency: Clear authority bands must link failure severity, available remedies and escalation responsibility.
controls.risk: Unempowered agents extend customer effort even when the failure and appropriate remedy are already known.
controls.kpi: Proposed KPI: time to remedy, escalation rate and recovery satisfaction.

gaps.label: 1 · Knowledge
gaps.definition: Customer expectations and management’s understanding of them do not fully align.
gaps.diagnostic: National averages can hide indoor, corridor and local installation variability.
gaps.symptom: A customer reports a persistent local problem while aggregate performance appears acceptable.
gaps.cause: A plausible cause is insufficient connection between local customer feedback and operational telemetry.
gaps.correction: Combine circle or cluster voice-of-customer analysis with relevant network and provisioning evidence.
gaps.kpi: Proposed KPI: locally classified complaints and the share linked to relevant diagnostic evidence.

gaps.label: 2 · Standards
gaps.definition: Management’s understanding of customer needs is not fully translated into service standards.
gaps.diagnostic: Meeting regulatory compliance requirements does not by itself establish premium end-to-end experience.
gaps.symptom: A service meets a minimum benchmark while customers still encounter effortful or inconsistent journeys.
gaps.cause: A plausible cause is the absence of explicit internal objectives for the experience promised to premium segments.
gaps.correction: Define measurable network, provisioning, support and recovery objectives above applicable minimum requirements where needed.
gaps.kpi: Proposed KPI: attainment of defined postpaid experience and recovery objectives.

gaps.label: 3 · Delivery
gaps.definition: Actual delivery falls short of the service standards the organization intends to meet.
gaps.diagnostic: Congestion, billing lags, provisioning defects and field delays can break otherwise sound service designs.
gaps.symptom: An accepted payment, plan change or installation promise fails to produce the expected service.
gaps.cause: A plausible cause is a broken cross-system handoff or an exception without an accountable owner.
gaps.correction: Use closed-loop assurance to enrich or trigger service cases from relevant operational events.
gaps.kpi: Proposed KPI: exception rate, entitlement success and installation on the committed date.

gaps.label: 4 · Communication
gaps.definition: The experience communicated to customers differs from what the service can deliver in their context.
gaps.diagnostic: A broad premium claim may exceed actual local coverage, device capability or plan eligibility.
gaps.symptom: A customer expects a promoted feature that their device or location cannot support.
gaps.cause: A plausible cause is conditional product language that is difficult to find or interpret before purchase.
gaps.correction: Place device and location checks with the offer and explain conditions in plain language.
gaps.kpi: Proposed KPI: eligibility-check accuracy and expectation-related complaints.

gaps.label: 5 · Perception
gaps.definition: The customer’s expected experience differs from their perceived experience.
gaps.diagnostic: Premium positioning may raise the reference point against which a customer judges everyday service.
gaps.symptom: Customers may judge an apparently acceptable technical result as poor value after repeated effort or weak recovery.
gaps.cause: A plausible cause is the combined effect of mismatched expectations, delivery failures and unresolved customer effort.
gaps.correction: Run expectation and perception studies alongside customer-effort and post-recovery measurement.
gaps.kpi: Proposed KPI: validated perception and expectation measures, effort and post-recovery satisfaction.

stages.title: Discover & choose
stages.job: Choose a mobile plan that fits everyday usage and device needs.
stages.touchpoint: The plan comparison page, app or retail conversation explains features and conditions.
stages.failure: Plan complexity, OTT conditions or unclear 5G eligibility create confusion before purchase.
stages.dependency: The offer catalogue must reflect actual device, location and entitlement conditions.
stages.impact: The customer begins the relationship with an expectation the selected plan may not meet.
stages.recovery: Offer an eligibility-led comparison and explain feature limits before commitment.

stages.title: KYC & port-in
stages.job: Move to the operator and activate service with a clear view of progress.
stages.touchpoint: Digital onboarding, the retail desk and activation notifications guide the transfer.
stages.failure: A KYC exception, porting delay or database mismatch leaves activation status unclear.
stages.dependency: Identity checks, porting workflows and provisioning records must maintain consistent order state.
stages.impact: Uncertainty prompts anxiety and repeated contact before the service relationship is established.
stages.recovery: Provide one activation tracker, proactive status updates and a named exception owner.

stages.title: First 5G use
stages.job: Use the high-value network feature promised with the plan.
stages.touchpoint: The customer’s device, network indicator and operator app make readiness visible.
stages.failure: Device incompatibility, outdated software, limited local coverage or a missing entitlement blocks access.
stages.dependency: Radio coverage, device configuration, plan eligibility and provisioning must all be ready.
stages.impact: An unavailable feature can create an immediate perception that the promise was not delivered.
stages.recovery: Provide a device and eligibility pre-check with specific corrective steps and assisted escalation.

stages.title: Routine use
stages.job: Rely on everyday calls, streaming and work across the places that matter.
stages.touchpoint: Daily network use and issue reporting expose the customer’s local experience.
stages.failure: Indoor congestion, dropped sessions, weak handovers or local degradation interrupt routine use.
stages.dependency: Cell-level experience monitoring and usable complaint diagnostics must identify persistent local issues.
stages.impact: Repeated inconsistency can erode trust and increase consideration of switching.
stages.recovery: Use relevant local diagnostics, communicate the incident status and verify restoration with the customer.

stages.title: Payment → benefit
stages.job: Pay for a recharge or plan and receive its benefits without delay or duplication.
stages.touchpoint: The payment receipt and app balance show whether the purchase has completed.
stages.failure: Money is debited while the purchased benefit remains absent.
stages.dependency: Payment confirmation, billing and entitlement systems must reconcile the same transaction.
stages.impact: The customer loses access or available funds and may repeat the payment unnecessarily.
stages.recovery: Show payment status, reconcile automatically and restore the benefit or reverse the transaction where appropriate.

stages.title: Understand the bill
stages.job: Understand current charges, renewal conditions and changes from the previous bill.
stages.touchpoint: The itemized bill, renewal notice and dispute flow explain what the customer owes.
stages.failure: An unexpected pack charge or unclear renewal appears without a usable explanation.
stages.dependency: Tariff records, renewal events and billing history must be available in a common view.
stages.impact: Unexplained charges reduce confidence and create avoidable dispute effort.
stages.recovery: Provide a plain-language line-item breakdown, historical context and an accessible dispute owner.

stages.title: Redeem a benefit
stages.job: Activate the OTT subscription or reward included with the chosen service.
stages.touchpoint: The operator app and partner redemption page hand the customer into the bundled service.
stages.failure: A partner API or entitlement integration fails despite the customer being eligible.
stages.dependency: Operator and partner systems must agree on customer eligibility and redemption status.
stages.impact: The bundle’s perceived value falls as the customer is passed between organizations.
stages.recovery: Keep end-to-end case ownership with the operator and coordinate the partner correction internally.

stages.title: Confirm feasibility
stages.job: Know whether broadband can be installed at the address before making a firm commitment.
stages.touchpoint: The availability checker, order confirmation and installation date set the initial expectation.
stages.failure: An order or payment is accepted before local physical feasibility is confirmed.
stages.dependency: Address validation, local capacity and field feasibility checks must inform order promises.
stages.impact: An uncertain installation date leaves the customer waiting for a service that may not be deliverable.
stages.recovery: Validate feasibility first and provide realistic dates, clear order state and a cancellation path when needed.

stages.title: Keep the appointment
stages.job: Have the installation completed during the agreed visit window.
stages.touchpoint: Appointment confirmations, engineer updates and rescheduling controls coordinate the visit.
stages.failure: A scheduling or dispatch problem causes an engineer no-show or unannounced delay.
stages.dependency: Field capacity, dispatch state and customer notifications must remain synchronized.
stages.impact: The customer loses time and must reorganize work or household commitments.
stages.recovery: Warn before a likely missed visit, enable self-rescheduling and apply a proportionate remedy where appropriate.

stages.title: Verify room coverage
stages.job: Use the installed connection reliably in the rooms where connectivity is needed.
stages.touchpoint: Router placement, the installation walkthrough and customer sign-off demonstrate readiness.
stages.failure: Poor placement, weak room coverage or incomplete testing leaves a technically active but disappointing service.
stages.dependency: The installer needs a room-coverage checklist, appropriate equipment placement and a documented closeout.
stages.impact: Customers may attribute an in-home Wi-Fi problem to the entire broadband service.
stages.recovery: Validate coverage with the customer, correct workmanship and verify the result before closing the visit.

recovery.label: Friction
recovery.response: Correct digitally first and transfer seamlessly to assisted support when the attempt does not resolve the issue.
recovery.remedy: Give an immediate explanation and a usable in-app correction.
recovery.kpi: Proposed KPI: digital containment and repeat contact within 24 hours.
recovery.distributive: Restore the expected function or give a clear explanation that addresses the actual confusion.
recovery.procedural: Keep correction short and preserve context if the customer needs assisted help.
recovery.interactional: Use respectful language and acknowledge the inconvenience without blaming the customer.

recovery.label: Material failure
recovery.response: Assign one case owner, diagnose the relevant backend issue and send proactive progress updates.
recovery.remedy: Restore service or access and consider a proportionate credit or validity extension where appropriate.
recovery.kpi: Proposed KPI: p90 time to resolution and repeat contact within seven days.
recovery.distributive: Match the restoration and any credit to the documented loss of access, time or value.
recovery.procedural: Provide a transparent case timeline and let the owner coordinate internal or partner handoffs.
recovery.interactional: Explain the failure competently, acknowledge its impact and take responsibility for the next step.

recovery.label: Critical failure
recovery.response: Use high-priority incident handling, bypass repetitive scripts and conduct formal root-cause analysis.
recovery.remedy: Provide a clear explanation, proportionate compensation and verified restoration.
recovery.kpi: Proposed KPI: root-cause closure and observed churn or port-out at 30 and 60 days.
recovery.distributive: Match the remedy to the failure’s duration, severity and documented customer impact.
recovery.procedural: Give a responsible escalation owner and verify recovery before closing the incident.
recovery.interactional: Recognize the accumulated effort and communicate honestly about progress and remaining uncertainty.

rules.title: One case, one history
rules.description: Preserve customer context across channels to support procedural fairness and respectful ownership.

rules.title: Detect before explaining
rules.description: Identify network or payment failures proactively where technically possible so the customer carries less diagnostic effort.

rules.title: Restore first, analyze later
rules.description: Restore usable service promptly without making unnecessary diagnostic steps a condition of a fair outcome.

rules.title: Harm-matched compensation
rules.description: Match the remedy to severity, duration and impact so the recovery outcome is proportionate.

rules.title: Active verification
rules.description: Confirm restoration with relevant checks and customer context before treating the case as resolved.

rules.title: Structural root-cause learning
rules.description: Aggregate recurring failures and remove their causes to improve the fairness and reliability of future recovery.

roadmap.title: Formal SERVQUAL Field Studies
roadmap.rationale: Network telemetry cannot directly measure empathy or assurance, and the supplied instrument leaves expectation and construct-validation gaps.
roadmap.dependency: Agree on questionnaire wording, expectation measures, sampling design and construct validation before fieldwork.
roadmap.kpi: Proposed KPI: sample adequacy, construct reliability and clearly defined perception and expectation measures.
roadmap.impact: Intended outcome: a stronger basis for judging service dimensions and choosing interventions.

roadmap.title: Establish Postpaid SLOs
roadmap.rationale: Premium postpaid positioning needs observable objectives across network, provisioning, support and recovery.
roadmap.dependency: Establish baseline measures in months 1–3 before piloting service objectives in months 4–6.
roadmap.kpi: Proposed KPI: customer effort, postpaid churn, repeat contact, p90 recovery time and entitlement success.
roadmap.impact: Intended outcome: premium value becomes testable across the complete customer journey.

roadmap.title: Close the Local Reliability Gap
roadmap.rationale: Jio’s lead in the cited national reliability and consistency measures motivates local diagnosis rather than assumptions about every location.
roadmap.dependency: Use local diagnostics to select pilots in months 2–6 and expand only after reviewing their results in months 7–12.
roadmap.kpi: Proposed KPI: circle or cluster reliability differences, complaints per 10,000 subscribers and indoor experience.
roadmap.impact: Intended outcome: investment addresses the local service inconsistencies customers actually experience.

roadmap.title: Frontline Recovery Empowerment
roadmap.rationale: Defined remedy authority can reduce unnecessary escalation for recurring classes of service failure.
roadmap.dependency: Agree on severity policy and remedy authority before a months 3–6 pilot and evidence-led expansion in months 7–12.
roadmap.kpi: Proposed KPI: time to remedy, recovery satisfaction, escalation rate and post-failure churn.
roadmap.impact: Intended outcome: capable frontline ownership makes recovery easier and more proportionate.

roadmap.title: Complaint-to-Network Closed Loop
roadmap.rationale: Linking cases to relevant network, provisioning or billing context can reduce the diagnostic burden carried by customers.
roadmap.dependency: Provide common case identifiers and telemetry access, then classify actual complaint causes before prioritising integrations.
roadmap.kpi: Proposed KPI: automatically enriched tickets, scripted troubleshooting cycles and time to identify a root cause.
roadmap.impact: Intended outcome: care teams receive the evidence needed to route and resolve exceptions more effectively.

roadmap.title: Engineer Zero-Repeat Journeys
roadmap.rationale: Payment, entitlement, installation and channel handoffs expose customers to avoidable repeat effort when system state breaks.
roadmap.dependency: Map the selected journeys and assign an exception owner before redesigning their weakest handoffs.
roadmap.kpi: Proposed KPI: exception rate, repeat contact, installation on the committed date and payment-to-entitlement success.
roadmap.impact: Intended outcome: fewer broken handoffs require customers to repeat the same request.

conclusions.airtel: Higher reported mobile ARPU supports the premiumisation narrative without measuring service quality directly.
conclusions.jio: Lower reported mobile ARPU accompanies a strategy built around scale and ecosystem value.

conclusions.airtel: Airtel has the smaller of the two TRAI-reported total broadband subscription bases in July 2026.
conclusions.jio: Jio has the larger TRAI-reported total broadband subscription base in the same reporting period.
conclusions.status: Regulatory evidence; the total includes M2M and is broader than household broadband.

conclusions.airtel: Airtel trails Jio in the cited national Reliability Experience, Consistent Quality and Download Speed Experience measures.
conclusions.jio: Jio leads these specific national measures in the February 2026 Opensignal report.
conclusions.status: Independent measurement; October–December 2025 observations do not describe every local experience.

conclusions.airtel: Airtel leads the cited 5G Upload Speed, Games Experience and Voice App Experience measures.
conclusions.jio: Jio’s strengths on other measured dimensions do not establish universal network superiority.
conclusions.status: Independent measurement; each metric retains its own definition and scale.

conclusions.airtel: Interpret Airtel’s ratings item by item with eligible counts, effect sizes and uncertainty.
conclusions.jio: Apply the same eligibility and inference rules to Jio before judging any observed difference.
conclusions.status: Workbook calculations; no validated overall SERVQUAL score or representative national satisfaction claim.

conclusions.airtel: The premium proposition creates a strategic need for low-effort support and empowered recovery.
conclusions.jio: The larger service footprint creates a strategic need for scalable exception handling and context continuity.
conclusions.status: Managerial inference; comparable public operational recovery metrics are insufficient for a ranking.

conclusions.airtel: Make premium value observable through local reliability, process discipline, clear eligibility and owned recovery.
conclusions.jio: Protect ecosystem value by keeping exceptions, service recovery and channel handoffs coherent at scale.
conclusions.status: Recommendation; intended benefits require measurement after implementation.
